meta.subject: GEOMETRY
meta.author: bank-team-geometry
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.learningObjective: Compute the area of a rectangle from its side lengths
questions.stem: A historical case describes a rectangular field 7 units by 4 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals length times width: 7 times 4 equals 28. Adding gives 11.

questions.learningObjective: Find area by counting unit squares
questions.stem: A historical grid contains 36 unit squares with no gaps; what is its area?

options.text: The area is 36 square units, one per unit square.
The area is 18 square units, half the square count.
The area is 72 square units, doubling the count.
The area is 6 square units, taking the square root.

questions.explanation: Each unit square contributes one square unit, so 36 squares give area 36. No further computation is needed.
questions.hint: One square equals one square unit.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the area of a parallelogram from base and height
questions.stem: A historical parallelogram has base 9 units and height 5 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals base times height: 9 times 5 equals 45. Using slant side instead of height would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the area of a trapezoid from its bases and height
questions.stem: A historical trapezoid has bases 6 and 10 units and height 4 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals half times (6+10) times 4 equals 32. Multiplying 6 by 10 would be wrong.
questions.hint: Average the bases, then multiply by height.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the area of a kite from its diagonals
questions.stem: A historical kite has diagonals 8 and 6 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals half the product of the diagonals: 0.5 times 8 times 6 equals 24. Adding 8 and 6 would be wrong.
questions.hint: Half the product of the diagonals.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the area of a triangle from base and height
questions.stem: A historical triangle has base 12 units and height 7 units; what is its area?

options.text: The area is 84 square units, omitting the half factor.
The area is 42 square units, half of 12 times 7.
The area is 19 square units, adding base and height.
The area is 5 square units, subtracting height from base.

questions.explanation: Triangle area equals half base times height: 0.5 times 12 times 7 equals 42. Omitting half would double it.
questions.hint: Multiply base by height, then halve.

questions.learningObjective: Compute composite area by addition
questions.stem: A historical figure is a 6 by 4 rectangle plus a 3 by 2 rectangle; what is its total area?
questions.explanation: First area is 24 and second is 6, so total is 30. Multiplying dimensions together would be wrong.

questions.topic: Composite area with a curved cut
questions.learningObjective: Compute area of a rectangle with a semicircular cutout
questions.stem: A historical 10 by 6 rectangle has a semicircle of radius 2 removed from one side; what is the remaining area? Use pi as 3.14.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 60 and semicircle area is 0.5 times 3.14 times 4 equals 6.28, so remaining is 53.72. Adding the cutout would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Compare areas of different shapes with same dimensions
questions.stem: A historical case asks whether a 4 by 6 rectangle and a parallelogram with base 4 and height 6 have equal area; what is true?

options.text: The parallelogram is larger, because of its slanted sides.
The rectangle is larger, because parallelograms are slanted.
They have equal area, since both are base times height.
They cannot be compared without side lengths.

questions.explanation: Both areas equal base times height, so they are equal. Slant does not change the perpendicular height.
questions.hint: Area depends on base and perpendicular height.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the new area after scaling a figure
questions.stem: A historical square of area 9 is scaled by factor 2; what is the new area?
questions.explanation: Area scales by square of factor, so 9 times 4 equals 36. Multiplying by 2 would give 18.

questions.topic: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.learningObjective: Compute the surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A historical triangular prism has two triangular bases of area 6 each and three rectangular faces with total area 30; what is its surface area?
questions.explanation: Surface area equals two bases plus lateral: 12 plus 30 equals 42. Using one base would give 36.
questions.hint: Add both bases and the lateral area.

questions.topic: Surface area of a prism with a trapezoidal base
questions.learningObjective: Compute the surface area of a prism with trapezoidal base
questions.stem: A historical prism has trapezoidal bases of area 10 each and lateral area 40; what is its surface area?

options.text: The surface area is 80 square units, doubling lateral.
The surface area is 50 square units, using one base.
The surface area is 40 square units, using lateral only.
The surface area is 60 square units, 20 plus 40.

questions.explanation: Surface area equals two bases plus lateral: 20 plus 40 equals 60. Using one base or only lateral would be wrong.

questions.topic: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.learningObjective: Compute the surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A historical box measures 3 by 4 by 5 units; what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Surface area equals 2(12+15+20) equals 94. Summing pairs once gives 47.
questions.hint: Double the sum of pair products.

questions.topic: Total surface area of a cylinder
questions.learningObjective: Compute the total surface area of a cylinder
questions.stem: A historical cylinder has radius 3 units and height 5 units; what is its total surface area? Use pi as 3.14.
questions.explanation: Lateral area is 2 times 3.14 times 3 times 5 equals 94.2 and two bases are 56.52, total 150.72. Lateral only would give 94.2.
questions.hint: Add lateral area to both bases.

questions.learningObjective: Compute surface area of a composite solid
questions.stem: A historical solid is two 2 by 2 by 2 cubes joined face to face; what is its surface area?
questions.explanation: One cube area is 24, two cubes 48, minus two joined faces 8 gives 40. Adding without subtracting gives 48.

questions.learningObjective: Convert square units to a larger area unit
questions.stem: A historical plot has area 10000 square centimeters; how many square meters is that?

options.text: The area is 100 square meters, dividing by 100.
The area is 1 square meter, dividing by 10000.
The area is 10000 square meters, no conversion.
The area is 0.01 square meters, dividing by 1,000,000.

questions.explanation: One square meter equals 10000 square centimeters, so divide 10000 by 10000 to get 1. Using 100 would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the error in a trapezoid area calculation
questions.stem: A historical memo computes trapezoid area as (b1+b2)*h without half; what is the error?

options.text: The memo uses the wrong height.
The memo adds the bases incorrectly.
The memo omits the factor of one-half.
The memo multiplies instead of adds.

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is half times (b1+b2) times h, so omitting half doubles the result. The sum and height are fine.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the error when using slant side as height
questions.stem: A historical memo uses the slant side length as the height of a parallelogram; what is the error?

options.text: The memo halves the area.
The memo uses base instead of height.
The memo doubles the height.
The memo uses slant length instead of perpendicular height.

questions.explanation: Parallelogram area uses perpendicular height, not slant side length. The slant side is longer than the height.
questions.hint: Height must be perpendicular to the base.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish area from perimeter
questions.stem: A historical case asks which measure is found by multiplying side lengths; what is it?

options.text: Multiplying side lengths finds perimeter.
Multiplying side lengths finds area, not perimeter.
Multiplying side lengths finds volume.
Multiplying side lengths finds diagonal.

questions.explanation: Area is found by multiplying dimensions, while perimeter is found by adding side lengths. Volume requires three dimensions.

questions.learningObjective: Compute area of union of two overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: Two historical rectangles have areas 20 and 15 and overlap in 5 square units; what is the union area?
questions.explanation: Union area equals 20 plus 15 minus 5 equals 30. Adding without subtracting overlap gives 35.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the error in a cylinder surface area calculation
questions.stem: A historical memo computes cylinder surface area as 2 pi r h only; what is the error?

options.text: The memo adds instead of multiplies.
The memo uses diameter instead of radius.
The memo omits the two circular bases.
The memo uses height squared.

questions.explanation: Total surface area includes lateral area plus two bases, so omitting bases leaves only lateral area. The radius and multiplication are fine.

questions.learningObjective: Compute actual area from a scale drawing
questions.stem: A historical scale drawing has area 12 square units with scale 1 to 3; what is the actual area?
questions.explanation: Area scale factor is 9, so actual area is 12 times 9 equals 108. Using scale 3 gives 36.
questions.hint: Square the scale factor for area.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize that rearranging preserves area
questions.stem: A historical case rearranges a parallelogram into a rectangle; what happens to the area?

options.text: The area becomes the perimeter.
The area increases when rearranged.
The area decreases when rearranged.
The area stays the same under rearrangement.

questions.explanation: Rearranging pieces preserves area, so the rectangle has the same area as the parallelogram. No area is added or removed.

questions.learningObjective: Compute trapezoid area using midsegment
questions.stem: A historical trapezoid has midsegment 8 units and height 5 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals midsegment times height: 8 times 5 equals 40. This equals half times (b1+b2) times h.

questions.learningObjective: Select the correct area formula for a shape
questions.stem: A historical case has a shape with two pairs of parallel sides and height 4; which formula gives its area?

options.text: Use half times base times height, as for a triangle.
Use base times height, since it is a parallelogram.
Use pi r squared, as for a circle.
Use side squared, as for a square.

questions.explanation: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides is a parallelogram, whose area is base times height. Triangle, circle, and square formulas do not apply.
questions.hint: Two pairs of parallel sides mean parallelogram.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the change in area when dimensions change
questions.stem: A historical rectangle changes from 5 by 4 to 6 by 4; by how much does its area increase?
questions.explanation: Old area is 20 and new area is 24, so increase is 4. Multiplying 1 by 4 gives the same result here.
questions.hint: Subtract old area from new area.

questions.learningObjective: Find a missing side from area and the other side
questions.stem: A historical rectangle has area 48 square units and width 6 units; what is its length?
questions.explanation: Length equals area divided by width: 48 over 6 equals 8. Multiplying 48 by 6 would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Compute rectangle area with fractional sides
questions.stem: A historical rectangle measures 2.5 by 4 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals 2.5 times 4 equals 10. Rounding 2.5 to 2 would give 8.

questions.learningObjective: Compute parallelogram area with given base and height
questions.stem: A historical parallelogram has base 8 units and height 3 units; what is its area?

options.text: The area is 11 square units, adding base and height.
The area is 26 square units, adding 8 and 3 then multiplying by 2.
The area is 24 square units, 8 times 3.
The area is 64 square units, squaring the base.

questions.explanation: Area equals base times height: 8 times 3 equals 24. Adding or squaring would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Compute trapezoid area with decimal bases
questions.stem: A historical trapezoid has bases 5.5 and 8.5 units and height 4 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals half times 14 times 4 equals 28. Using 5.5 times 8.5 would be wrong.
questions.hint: Average the bases, then multiply by height.

questions.learningObjective: Compute kite area with given diagonals
questions.stem: A historical kite has diagonals 10 and 4 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals half times 10 times 4 equals 20. Multiplying without half gives 40.

questions.learningObjective: Compute triangle area with given base and height
questions.stem: A historical triangle has base 10 units and height 6 units; what is its area?

options.text: The area is 4 square units, subtracting height from base.
The area is 60 square units, omitting the half factor.
The area is 16 square units, adding base and height.
The area is 30 square units, half of 10 times 6.

questions.explanation: Triangle area equals half base times height: 0.5 times 10 times 6 equals 30. Omitting half doubles it.
questions.hint: Multiply base by height, then halve.

questions.learningObjective: Compute composite area by subtraction
questions.stem: A historical 8 by 5 rectangle has a 2 by 2 square removed; what is the remaining area?
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 40 and removed square is 4, so remaining is 36. Adding gives 44.

questions.topic: Composite area with a curved cut
questions.learningObjective: Compute area of rectangle with semicircular top
questions.stem: A historical 6 by 4 rectangle has a semicircle of radius 2 added on top; what is the total area? Use pi as 3.14.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 24 and semicircle area is 6.28, total 30.28. Subtracting would give 17.72.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if two triangles with same base and height have equal area
questions.stem: A historical case compares two triangles with the same base 8 and height 5; what is true about their areas?

options.text: The taller-looking one is larger.
They have equal area, since both are half base times height.
They cannot be equal unless congruent.
The one with longer sides is larger.

questions.explanation: Triangle area depends only on base and height, so equal base and height give equal area. Shape does not matter.
questions.hint: Area depends on base and height only.

questions.learningObjective: Compute area scale factor from length scale factor
questions.stem: A historical figure is scaled by factor 3; by what factor does its area change?
questions.explanation: Area scales by square of length scale factor, so 3 squared equals 9. Multiplying by 3 would be linear.

questions.topic: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.learningObjective: Compute surface area with given base and lateral areas
questions.stem: A historical triangular prism has two bases of area 5 each and lateral area 24; what is its surface area?

options.text: The surface area is 24 square units, lateral only.
The surface area is 29 square units, using one base.
The surface area is 34 square units, 10 plus 24.
The surface area is 39 square units, adding an extra base.

questions.explanation: Surface area equals two bases plus lateral: 10 plus 24 equals 34. Using one base or only lateral would be wrong.

questions.topic: Surface area of a prism with a trapezoidal base
questions.learningObjective: Compute surface area with trapezoidal bases
questions.stem: A historical prism has trapezoidal bases of area 12 each and lateral area 36; what is its surface area?
questions.explanation: Surface area equals two bases plus lateral: 24 plus 36 equals 60. Using one base gives 48.

questions.topic: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.learningObjective: Compute surface area with given dimensions
questions.stem: A historical box measures 2 by 3 by 4 units; what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Surface area equals 2(6+8+12) equals 52. Summing pairs once gives 26.
questions.hint: Double the sum of pair products.

questions.topic: Total surface area of a cylinder
questions.learningObjective: Compute total surface area of a cylinder
questions.stem: A historical cylinder has radius 2 units and height 4 units; what is its total surface area? Use pi as 3.14.

options.text: The total is about 100.48 square units, doubling lateral.
The total is about 50.24 square units, lateral only.
The total is about 25.12 square units, one base only.
The total is about 75.36 square units, 50.24 plus 25.12.

questions.explanation: Lateral area is 50.24 and two bases are 25.12, total 75.36. Lateral only would give 50.24.
questions.hint: Add lateral area to both bases.

questions.learningObjective: Compute surface area of composite solid
questions.stem: Two 1 by 1 by 1 cubes are glued face to face; what is the surface area of the resulting solid?
questions.explanation: One cube area is 6, two cubes 12, minus two glued faces 2 gives 10. Adding without subtracting gives 12.

questions.learningObjective: Convert square meters to square centimeters
questions.stem: A historical plot has area 3 square meters; how many square centimeters is that?
questions.explanation: One square meter equals 10000 square centimeters, so 3 times 10000 equals 30000. Using 100 would give 300.

questions.learningObjective: Identify error in trapezoid area with wrong bases
questions.stem: A historical memo uses only one base times height for a trapezoid; what is the error?

options.text: The memo uses the wrong height.
The memo ignores the second base and the half factor.
The memo adds the bases incorrectly.
The memo multiplies the bases.

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area requires both bases averaged and the half factor, so using one base is wrong. Height and addition are fine.

questions.learningObjective: Identify error when using a side as height
questions.stem: A historical memo uses the length of a non-perpendicular side as the height of a parallelogram; what is the error?

options.text: The memo doubles the height.
The memo uses the base as height.
The memo uses a slant side instead of perpendicular height.
The memo halves the area.

questions.explanation: Parallelogram area needs perpendicular height, not a slant side. The slant side overestimates the height.

questions.learningObjective: Identify which operation gives perimeter
questions.stem: A historical case asks which operation finds the perimeter of a rectangle; what is it?

options.text: Dividing sides finds perimeter.
Multiplying side lengths finds perimeter.
Squaring one side finds perimeter.
Adding all side lengths finds perimeter.

questions.explanation: Perimeter is the sum of all side lengths, while area is the product of dimensions. Multiplication gives area.

questions.learningObjective: Compute intersection area from union and individual areas
questions.stem: Two historical rectangles have areas 25 and 20 and union area 35; what is their overlap?
questions.explanation: Overlap equals 25 plus 20 minus 35 equals 10. Adding union would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Identify error in cylinder surface area using diameter as radius
questions.stem: A historical memo computes cylinder surface area using diameter as radius; what is the error?

options.text: The memo should double the height.
The memo should halve the diameter to get radius.
The memo should omit pi.
The memo should add radius and height.

questions.explanation: Cylinder formulas use radius, so diameter must be halved. The height and pi are correct.

questions.learningObjective: Compute drawing area from actual area and scale
questions.stem: A historical actual field has area 225 square units with scale 1 to 5; what is the drawing area?
questions.explanation: Drawing area equals actual area divided by 25: 225 over 25 equals 9. Dividing by 5 gives 45.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize area preservation under dissection
questions.stem: A historical case cuts a triangle and rearranges it into a parallelogram; what happens to the area?

options.text: The area decreases after rearrangement.
The area increases after rearrangement.
The area stays the same under dissection.
The area becomes the perimeter.

questions.explanation: Dissection and rearrangement preserve area, so the parallelogram has the same area as the triangle. No area is lost.

questions.learningObjective: Find height from area and midsegment
questions.stem: A historical trapezoid has area 48 square units and midsegment 8 units; what is its height?
questions.explanation: Height equals area divided by midsegment: 48 over 8 equals 6. Multiplying gives 384.

questions.learningObjective: Select area formula for a trapezoid
questions.stem: A historical case has a quadrilateral with one pair of parallel sides and height 5; which formula gives its area?

options.text: Use side squared, as for a square.
Use base times height, as for a parallelogram.
Use half times base times height, as for a triangle.
Use half times sum of bases times height, since it is a trapezoid.

questions.explanation: A quadrilateral with one pair of parallel sides is a trapezoid, whose area is half times (b1+b2) times h. Other formulas do not apply.
questions.hint: One pair of parallel sides means trapezoid.

questions.learningObjective: Compute new area after scaling dimensions
questions.stem: A historical rectangle 4 by 5 is scaled by factor 2 in both dimensions; what is the new area?
questions.explanation: New dimensions are 8 and 10, area 80. Adding scale factor to area 20 would give 22.

questions.learningObjective: Find missing side of trapezoid from area
questions.stem: A historical trapezoid has area 30, height 5, and one base 4; what is the other base?
questions.explanation: Area equals half times (4+x) times 5, so 30 equals 2.5(4+x), giving x equals 8. Using full product would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Compute rectangle area with given side lengths
questions.stem: A historical rectangle measures 9 by 2 units; what is its area?

options.text: The area is 11 square units, adding 9 and 2.
The area is 18 square units, 9 times 2.
The area is 81 square units, squaring 9.
The area is 7 square units, subtracting 2 from 9.

questions.explanation: Area equals length times width: 9 times 2 equals 18. Adding or squaring would be wrong.

questions.learningObjective: Find base from area and height
questions.stem: A historical parallelogram has area 54 square units and height 6 units; what is its base?
questions.explanation: Base equals area divided by height: 54 over 6 equals 9. Multiplying gives 324.

questions.learningObjective: Compute trapezoid area with given bases and height
questions.stem: A historical trapezoid has bases 7 and 9 units and height 4 units; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals half times 16 times 4 equals 32. Using 7 times 9 would be wrong.
questions.hint: Average the bases, then multiply by height.

questions.learningObjective: Find a diagonal from area and other diagonal
questions.stem: A historical kite has area 30 square units and one diagonal 5 units; what is the other diagonal?

options.text: The other diagonal is 150 units, multiplying 30 by 5.
The other diagonal is 6 units, dividing 30 by 5.
The other diagonal is 12 units, since 2 times 30 divided by 5 equals 12.
The other diagonal is 25 units, subtracting 5 from 30.

questions.explanation: Area equals half d1 d2, so d2 equals 2 times 30 over 5 equals 12. Omitting the 2 gives 6.
questions.hint: Multiply area by 2, then divide by the known diagonal.

questions.learningObjective: Find height from area and base
questions.stem: A historical triangle has area 24 square units and base 8 units; what is its height?
questions.explanation: Height equals 2 times area over base: 48 over 8 equals 6. Dividing 24 by 8 gives 3, which is wrong.
questions.hint: Multiply area by 2, then divide by base.

questions.learningObjective: Compute composite area of rectangle and triangle
questions.stem: A historical figure is a 6 by 4 rectangle plus a triangle of base 6 and height 4; what is its total area?
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 24 and triangle area is 12, total 36. Adding dimensions would be wrong.

questions.topic: Composite area with a curved cut
questions.learningObjective: Compute area of rectangle with quarter circle removed
questions.stem: A historical 8 by 6 rectangle has a quarter circle of radius 2 removed from a corner; what is the approximate remaining area? Use pi as 3.14.

options.text: The remaining area is about 47.0 square units, rounding pi to 3.
The remaining area is about 46.43 square units, subtracting 1.57.
The remaining area is about 41.72 square units, subtracting a semicircle.
The remaining area is about 44.86 square units, 48 minus 3.14.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 48 and quarter circle area is 3.14, so remaining is 44.86. Using a semicircle or halving would be wrong.
questions.hint: Subtract one quarter of pi r squared.
